subject: Should you change the esmator from ML to DWLS in this case?

messages.author: 95f934d9584dabac
messages.subject: Should you change the esmator from ML to DWLS in this case?
parts:
Hi,
Yes, this might be a basic question but one of my friends want to hear that from the lavaan community or possibly from Yves himself.
In lavaan (and SEM in general), is it OK to use ML estimator when the exogenous variable, but not the endogenous variable, is categorical? My friend says that when any categorical variable is involved in SEM, one needs to use estimators other than ML such as DWLS or WLSM. However, my understanding is that as long as the categorical is an exogenous variable, ML (or its variants such as MLR) can be used.

Let me know what is the correct decision. 
Thanks!

messages.author: f1530326ce101401
messages.subject: Re: Should you change the esmator from ML to DWLS in this case?
parts:
Hi,

Indeed, it depends on whether your categorical variable is exogenous or endogenous. I believe it is not necessary in case of an exogenous categorical variable (but you need to recode as a dummy). In case of (an) endogenous categorical variable(s), you will need to declare the categorical variable(s) as ordered and then lavaan will automatically switch to the WLSMV estimator.

The information can be found on the tutorial page: https://lavaan.ugent.be/tutorial/cat.html

Best wishes,

Jasper

messages.author: bc810b1d0900407f
messages.subject: Re: Should you change the esmator from ML to DWLS in this case?
parts:
In case you need some references to read, you can try Chapter 11 of Kline (2016). The first paragraph of the section on ML (p. 235) is about the question you asked:

Kline, R. B. (2016). Principles and practice of structural equation modeling (4th Ed.). The Guilford Press.

You can also try pp. 126-127 of Bollen (1989):

Bollen, K. A. (1989). Structural equations with latent variables. Wiley-Interscience.

Hope this helps.

-- Shu Fai
